judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple "lesser of" formula, definite once the Borrowing Base is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.1(c) (c172) and the Borrowing Base definition (c035); the "subject to the terms and conditions" opener harmonises with 3.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reserve right runs to "such amounts, and with respect to such matters, as Lender in its Permitted Discretion shall deem necessary or appropriate", with items (i)-(iv) illustrative and (iii) and (iv) overlapping — an open-ended power against enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The sentence "Lender agrees not to establish any such reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred and is continuing" cuts across the unrestricted grant in the same clause and against the Borrowing Base definition (c035), which subtracts reserves without qualification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limb — availability plus cash in Cash Management Accounts may not exceed "the aggregate amount of unfunded commitments of Fund to the makers of Notes Receivable" — is a novel and awkwardly expressed cap whose operation is hard to read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a constraint not reflected in the Borrowing Base (c035), the Availability definition (c017) or the Overadvance provision (c179), so the three do not obviously line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard revolving reborrowing language; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.4 Term and 2.1(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, with "including without limitation the conditions set forth in Section 3.3"; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the condition structure in 3.3 (c237-c242); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed mechanics with an internal safety valve (failure to confirm telephonic notice does not affect validity); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 2.8, which lets Lender act on instructions from "anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person"; that is a deliberate allocation of risk rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite funding mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Funding "to the account of a Settlement Agent" fits 2.8's Designated Account default and the Settlement Agent definition (c149).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise cut-off times and deemed-receipt rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.7 Crediting Payments, which uses the same 1:00 p.m. Dallas cut-off.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-step waterfall drafted with precision; clause (iii)'s definition of "paid in full" and clause (ii)'s carve-out for specified payments are explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iv) expressly anticipates "actual, irreconcilable conflict" with other Loan Documents and resolves it in favour of 2.3, which both signals and manages a cross-document tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "greater than any of the limitations set forth in Section 2.1" is definite by reference; the second sentence is a general promise to pay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(c) contains two distinct limits and 2.3(b)(D) refers to Overadvances being "created"; the interplay is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clean rate alternatives keyed to defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Applicable Margin (c010), 2.12 LIBOR Option and the exclusion of Bank Product Obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "(and at the election of Lender)" leaves it unclear whether the default rate applies automatically or only if Lender elects, and whether an election must be communicated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1's remedies and 2.5(c)'s charging mechanic assume amounts become due automatically; the elective default rate is a small point of friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and definite, including express authority to compound unpaid interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 2.9 Loan Account and 2.10; the compounding is expressly qualified by the usury savings clause in 2.5(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 360-day/actual-days convention stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.5(a) and the Base Rate definition; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard usury savings clause; the "ipso facto, as of the date of this Agreement" phrasing is unusual but its effect is spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by the proviso in 2.10(e); the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) requires "all payments for each sale or other disposition of one or more Notes Receivable or payment in full ... to be made by the escrow company, title insurance company or refinancing lender or purchaser directly to a Cash Management Account" — a long compound sentence whose reach over sale proceeds, and the meaning of "Collections", is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Permitted Dispositions (c127)(e), which conditions note sales on proceeds being paid "directly to a Cash Management Account as provided in Section 2.6(a)", and with 4.9(b)'s release-on-sale mechanic; whether a sale outside the lockbox is nonetheless effective is a real whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prescribes required terms of the Cash Management Agreements with specificity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The required daily sweep to Lender's Account sits alongside 2.6(e)'s permission for Borrower to withdraw escrow funds daily; the escrow carve-out needs harmonising with the sweep.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "no longer acceptable in Lender's reasonable judgment" appears twice, but with concrete 30- and 60-day cure windows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.6(a)'s requirement that Wells Fargo be the sole Cash Management Bank after 60 days, though that requirement makes the amendment right in this clause largely theoretical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, clear grant of a Lien in the Cash Management Accounts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the grant in 4.1 over Deposit Accounts within Borrower Collateral (c032)(d); cumulative rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception for "accounts belonging to an Account Debtor of Borrower" is undefined in scope, and the clause calls the escrow account both an "Escrow Account" and a "Cash Management Account" in the same breath.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The permitted daily withdrawals conflict in practice with 2.6(b)(iii)'s requirement that all amounts in Cash Management Accounts be swept daily to Lender's Account, and Escrow Accounts are also Borrower Collateral under c032(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and definite deemed-receipt rules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 2.3(a)'s cut-off and 2.9's crediting of the Loan Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the duplicated words "agrees to establish establish", a plain typographical slip that does not change meaning; the risk-allocation for "anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person" is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.2(b)'s funding to the Designated Account and the Designated Account definition (c059).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account-stated mechanic with a 30-day objection window and "absent manifest error" is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 2.5(c)'s charging authority and 2.3's application rules; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar fee, fully earned on a stated date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the non-refundability preamble and 3.7's separate prepayment premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence omits the word "fee" ("a monthly loan administration equal to $2,000"), a mechanical slip that does not obscure the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of 2.10 and with 2.5(c)'s charging mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text says "one-half of one percent (0.30%)" — the words and the figure contradict each other, a mechanical error that changes the fee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Applicable Margin definition (c010) uses "one-half of one percent (0.50%)", confirming the figure here is wrong; the discrepancy is internal to the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "actual reasonable and customary charges" is a soft standard but the per-diem audit fee is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to the caps contemplated in Lender Expenses (c099)(c) and (g), which speak of "any limitation contained in this Agreement"; whether any such limitation exists is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed make-whole calculation with an explicit usury proviso; arithmetic and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with the unused line fee in 2.10(c), which also uses the $20,000,000 Minimum Interest Period floor, raising a question whether both charges apply to the same shortfall.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but conventional capital-adequacy language; "by any amount deemed by Lender to be material" and "any reasonable averaging and attribution methods" are soft but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "payable within 30 days" (OCR "$0 days") sits against "pay Lender on demand" in the same sentence, a small internal timing tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear mechanics for election, automatic conversion and Lender's rights on default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.12(b) and (c); the deemed-election default in (c) is the mirror image of this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise deadlines and confirmation requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Interest Period definition (c092) and 2.12(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed-election rule; the clause uses the singular "Borrower" where elsewhere the electing party is "Administrative Borrower".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(a) and (b) give the election to Administrative Borrower, while this clause deems "Borrower" to have elected; combined with c031's each/either rule, who elects is not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any change in market conditions" that makes it "impractical" in Lender's "reasonable opinion" is a notably loose trigger for converting all LIBOR loans.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.12(a)'s conversion mechanic and 2.12(e); no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, clear disclaimer of matched funding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the LIBOR Rate definition's reliance on quotation sources rather than actual funding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consideration recital for joint and several liability; conclusory but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports 2.13(b)-(k); the "mutual benefit" recital could be tested against the reality that only Fund holds the Notes Receivable, a recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "not merely as a surety but also as a co-debtor" is a precise and well-understood formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13(a), (c) and (d); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13(b)'s joint and several liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "irrespective of the validity, regularity or enforceability of this Agreement or any other circumstances whatsoever" is a sweeping catch-all that would, read literally, survive the Agreement's own invalidity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 16.4 Severability and the usury savings clause in 2.5(e), which contemplate that some terms may be unenforceable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long waiver list ending in "all demands, notices and other formalities of every kind", but bracketed by "except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The express carve-out reconciles it with the notice provisions elsewhere (e.g. 9.1 and 3.4); coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation and covenant about staying informed; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the waiver structure of 2.13(e) and Section 5's representations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to "Section S80(d) of the California Code of Civil Procedure" (580d) with an OCR slip, but the statutory reference is recoverable and the waiver is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 2.13(h)'s real property waivers, which cite 580a, 580b, 580d and 726; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii)(B) refers to "Agent and Lenders" although this is a single-lender facility with no agent, a drafting carry-over that misdescribes the parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The rest of the instrument consistently uses "Lender" in the singular and has no Agent; this stray plural is an internal inconsistency, albeit an obvious one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear enforcement and reinstatement language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors 16.7 Revival and Reinstatement of Obligations; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite subordination of contribution and subrogation claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13(k) and the "paid in full in cash" gloss in 2.3(b)(iii) and 1.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear trigger (after a Default or Event of Default) and trustee mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13(j) and the application waterfall in 2.3(b); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A condition precedent expressed with a deeming rule (funding conclusively deemed satisfaction or waiver) and a concrete deliverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4(a)'s filing authorisation and the Filing Authorization Letter definition (c076).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of documents, all defined terms; "satisfactory to Lender" is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Loan Documents definition (c110), though that definition also lists notes and "any other agreement" not required here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to attestation by "an Authorized Person" to resolutions of the "Board of Directors" and "specific officers" of LLC borrowers — corporate vocabulary applied to LLCs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Board of Directors definition (c029) expressly extends to comparable managers or managing members, which cures most of the mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Governing Documents definition (c081) and 5.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "dated within 36 days of the Closing Date" is almost certainly an OCR rendering of 30 days, and it differs from the 30-day period in the very next paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(f) (c220) uses 30 days for the same kind of certificate, so the two conditions are internally inconsistent as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions good standing on jurisdictions where failure to qualify "would constitute a Material Adverse Change", importing that vague standard into a documentary condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Material Adverse Change definition (c112) and mirrors 5.9; consistent in structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cross-referential and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8 Insurance supplies the required endorsements; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "in form and substance satisfactory to Lender" with no description of the opinion's content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Standard closing condition; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific as to what must be evidenced, with an express Permitted Protest carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Permitted Protest definition (c131) and 6.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long list of diligence items closed by "the results of which shall be satisfactory to Lender" — an entirely subjective condition attached to enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(r), (s) and (u), which use the same formula; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "satisfactory to Lender in its sole discretion" — an unqualified discretion standard, though as a closing condition it is spent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Uses the same four names as Permitted Holders (c128) rather than the five in Authorized Person (c016); minor list inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "shall have paid or shall pay with the initial Advance" states two alternatives without choosing, but the practical effect is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Lender Expenses (c099) and Section 10; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite documentary condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Borrower's Required Procedures definition (c033), which itself requires pre-Closing Lender approval.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar threshold measured by a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on Tangible Net Worth (c157), which adds back Subordinated Debt; whether the reorganization notes count toward the $600,000,000 is a live interaction with 7.16.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a single specific address; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relates to the Collateral Access Agreement definition (c049) and 7.15; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "been satisfied that such documentation provides Fund and Lender with appropriate rights and remedies" is a purely subjective satisfaction test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps 3.1(m)'s approval of the same form documents; duplicative rather than contradictory.
